newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed in dwindling trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed in dwindling trade.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mixed on Friday on dwindling volume and turnover, and traders said a gloomy period, marked by absence of foreign investors, was bound to last.
"Pessimism still reigns. There is no money as foreign buyers are staying away," said Marko Nikolac of Metroholding brokerage, but added he could not foresee any dramatic losses in the days ahead.
"How could (the prices) get possibly lower than this?," he asked.
Seven of 17 active issues rose, six fell and four were flat on Friday. Volume halved to 6,433 shares and turnover was more than three times lower at 4.8 million kuna.
Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka rebounded 40 kuna to its support point of 2,000 kuna on volume of 1,148 shares.
But traders described its closing price as "unrealistic" as it sold most shares in a 1,933-50 kuna range with few last deals struck at 2,000 kuna.

Zagrebacka E-series preference stock added 25 kuna to 1,200, with 906 shares sold. Traders noted the stock had been on a continuous rise, climbing 15 percent in two weeks, and said it was moving up to close the gap with bank's ordinary share.
"There are great expectations for E-series, as buying orders have piled up for it," one trader said.
Fully-listed drugs firm Pliva remained flat at 450 kuna, selling only 245 shares.
Nikolac said both Pliva and Zagrebacka were tracing developments of their Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) in London. In London, Pliva traded at $15.385 and Zagrebacka at $33 on Friday afternoon.
Most active food processor Podravka inched down 0.50 kuna to 279.50 on volume of 1,587 units.
Traders ascribed Podravka's bad performance to rumours that the firm's 1996 losses exceeded those of the year before.
Top gainer Karlovacka Banka's 2C-series gained 10 kuna to 260 on volume 1,300, in a first deal since March 6.
Biggest loser electric manufacturer Koncar fell 65 kuna to 1,200, selling 17 shares.
